correctness.rationale: For n=2,3 zero-sum real quartic identity is elementary. For n>=4 compact constrained extremization gives <=3 stationary coordinate levels; positive second variation at repeated outer roots excludes nonmaximal three-level patterns, leaving exact two-level k optimization and the universal real upper bound. Integrating all real parts of the complex vector gives a sharp complex upper bound. Cauchy--Schwarz and n-th roots of unity give a sharp complex lower bound. Permutation averaging of arbitrary complex Hermitian quadratic forms forces a scalar multiple of B and proves the exact complex BM optimum. The standalone exact checker validates algebraic angular coefficients and small-dimensional examples but is not the universal proof.
